Subject: Next steps & PR guidance — Coupa/Ariba supplier IDs + PO vs card

Hi Samir / Monica —

Great to meet earlier today — really appreciate the context on your platform rollout and the short pilot you have planned. Quick recap and suggested next steps so procurement can move forward without blockers: 

1) Commercial path (pilot vs long-term):
- If the initial pilot spend is under your corporate card threshold (typically <$10k), many customers use a card to move fast.
- For anything >$10k or for teams that require purchase orders and budget controls, you should create a Purchase Requisition (PR) and issue a PO.

2) Marketplace option:
- If you prefer minimal procurement overhead, Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace (link below). Purchasing via marketplace can let you bypass some vendor setup steps — happy to introduce you to our Marketplace rep if helpful.

3) Coupa / Ariba guidance & supplier IDs (to help your procurement team):
- Coupa: Vendor name = "Redwood Inference, Inc."; supplier ID: RDW-INF-1245.
- Ariba: Vendor ID = 100845-US; vendor name = "Redwood Inference".
- If your system requires a punchout, we don’t currently support punchout catalogs — procurement should add Redwood as a supplier using the details above.

4) PR creation checklist (attach to PR):
- Acme PR template (attached) filled with: legal entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.), estimated monthly/annual amount, cost center, GL code, and approver.
- Copy of the signed MSA or SOW (if you plan to reference terms).
- Supplier invoice remit address: Redwood Inference, Inc., 123 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105.
- Preferred invoice email: invoices@redwood.com

5) Internal ticketing / next steps on our side:
- Dev (cc’d) will open a supplier onboarding ticket with Finance Ops to confirm the IDs and add you as a reference if procurement needs a supplier request from Redwood.

Attachments: Acme_PR_Template.pdf, Redwood_Supplier_Instructions.docx (attached)

Action items:
- Samir / Monica: confirm whether you want to purchase via card (pilot) or start a PR/PO for the pilot. If PR, please send the PR number + the cost center and approver name.
- Marissa/Rishi/Dev: we'll standby to support supplier onboarding and provide any missing vendor paperwork.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if that helps accelerate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Samir / Monica —

Thanks — I’ll own the supplier onboarding on our side. A few notes and what I’ll do next: 

1) Supplier IDs:
- Coupa: "Redwood Inference, Inc." — supplier ID: RDW-INF-1245 (this is the ID that should appear in your vendor search).
- Ariba: vendor ID: 100845-US.

2) Vendor docs:
- I’ll attach our W-9 and vendor packet to the onboarding ticket (I’m adding them to the ticket now).

3) PR vs Card guidance:
- It’s fine to use a corp card for a small pilot; when you convert to a recurring/committed purchase we’ll coordinate to issue a PO to avoid midsubscription billing complications. Our billing team can accept card payments and later apply a credit against a PO when/if you switch — we’ll track that in the invoice.

4) What I need from you to open the PR on your side:
- Legal company name to match supplier setup (please confirm exactly how Acme Analytics lists itself in Coupa/Ariba).
- Estimated spend for the pilot and cost center/gl code.
- PR owner / approver name & email.

5) Internal ticket I’m opening: FIN-1023 (Finance Ops) — I’ll attach the W-9, vendor packet, and the signed SOW copy. I’ll also include the Redwood supplier IDs for quick reference.

If you send the legal name and PR owner, I’ll ping your procurement team inside the ticket and request expedited setup.

Thanks,
